AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: Seapunk.cs:46-49 overrides AfterAddedToRoom with a body of exactly `await base.AfterAddedToRoom();` - it adds nothing. The sim's constructor likewise only supplies the rng default. SHARED-FINDINGS section 2's constructor-applied-power divergence therefore does NOT arise for this unit, and copying that section's deliberate-divergence here would have been a false positive. This is the one AfterAddedToRoom in the batch that is genuinely faithful.

guards.rationale: SeapunkNormal.GenerateMonsters emits (CalcifiedCultist, null) then (Seapunk, null) (SeapunkNormal.cs:22-26) - the cultist FIRST - and the sim's SEAPUNK_NORMAL is [CalcifiedCultist, Seapunk] (seapunk.py:67-70). SeapunkWeak is the Seapunk alone on both sides. Neither encounter overrides Slots, so no slot sort applies.

guards.what: The port carries no `name` class attribute
guards.rationale: Presentation surface, waived per SHARED-FINDINGS section 4 (monster_state_machine N2/N5 and the KinPriest N6 precedent). Read to the end before waiving: Every other unit in this batch pins `name` (e.g. 'Fossil Stalker'); Seapunk does not. The conformance driver falls back to the class name (combat_driver.py:37-45, `getattr(monster, 'name', None) or type(monster).__name__`), which yields 'Seapunk' - the same single word the game displays - so no replay diverges today. Display-name only, and a tooling note rather than a fidelity finding, but flagged because the memory of this project records two multi-word names (Spiny Toad, Tough Egg) that DID break conformance for exactly this reason.
